title: Measure a reuse-ladder rule against a one-line YAGNI rule on screened units
body:
Source: operator link 2026-11-17 (Ponytail, https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail); disposition in .krn/runs/research/rss-dispositions.md. The vendor claims -53% code and -26% cost, self-measured, and a 7-word YAGNI prompt nearly matched it.
Outcome: one screen run over the S7 screened units compares three arm-A variants: no rule, a one-line YAGNI rule, and the Ponytail-style reuse ladder. It reports the median added lines per diff and the hidden-test pass rate per arm, with a per-unit table. The ladder goes to the brain only if it cuts added lines by at least 25% with a pass rate no lower than no rule.
Proof: the screen report prints both metrics per arm over at least 30 units, plus a keep/drop verdict line.
Files: evals/replay/arms.ts
